item.title: Omokri receives Mexico’s agrément as Nigeria’s Ambassador
item.description: Reno Omokri has received the agrément of the Government of Mexico for his appointment as Nigeria’s Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary to the country. Omokri disclosed this on his X platform on Wednesday, saying the Chargé d’Affaires of the Embassy of Mexico in Abuja, Mr José Manuel Briseño Flores, delivered the agrément to the Director of Protocol at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Babagana Wakil. The agrément formally signifies the Mexican government’s acceptance of Omokri’s appointment as Nigeria’s ambassador to Mexico. According to Omokri, his diplomatic assignment will also include concurrent accreditation to Guatemala, Honduras and Nicaragua. He announced the development in a post expressing gratitude to God, describing himself by his full name, Bemigho Reno Omokri, and confirming his designation as Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of the Federal Republic of Nigeria to the United Mexican States. item.title: 2027: APC campaign council reshuffles youth, women mobilisation teams
item.description: The PBAT/APC 2027 Presidential Campaign Council has announced changes to its leadership structure, including the creation of a directorate to oversee stage organisation and management ahead of the general elections. Imo State Governor and council secretary, Hope Uzodimma, announced the appointments in a statement on Monday, saying the changes were designed to improve coordination, strengthen the council’s structure and boost operational efficiency. Under the new arrangement, Farouk Aliyu will head the Directorate of Stage Organisation and Management, with Adejare Bello appointed as co-director. The council also named Youth Development Minister Ayodele Olawande as director of youth mobilisation, while Dayo Israel will serve as his deputy. For women mobilisation, Mary Aille Idele was appointed director, with Betta Edu as deputy director and Imaan Suleman as secretary. Uzodimma said the appointments were part of efforts to establish a coordinated and inclusive campaign structure capable of mobilising support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027. He said the appointees were expected to deploy their experience and organisational skills to their respective roles and collaborate with other directorates in implementing the council’s campaign and mobilisation plans. The changes come as the ruling All Progressives Congress prepares for the 2027 presidential election, with youth and women mobilisation identified as key components of its campaign strategy. item.title: Zamfara 2027: Governor Lawal, 14 other candidates sign peace accord
item.description: Governor Dauda Lawal of Zamfara State and 14 other governorship candidates yesterday signed a peace accord to ensure peace and order in the forthcoming 2027 General elections. The accord, organised by the Zamfara State Police Command in Gusau, was signed at the Peace Accord and Election Security Summit held in Zamfara State. The Peace Accord signing ceremony was meant to ensure peace and order for all political parties in the country as a preparation for free and fair 2027 elections. Governor Lawal, along with all contestants in the governorship, national and state assembly elections, were invited to sign and promise that no one will violate or work against any election processes before, during and after elections. The governor, as one of the contestants under the All Progressive Congress (APC), signed the accord and prayed for peace, free and fair elections, and all the political parties did the same. In his speech, Zamfara State Commissioner of Police, CP Ahmed Mohammed Bello Daga, called on all the contestants to shun, avoid, and not try to violate any election processes before, during and after elections. He warned that any political aspirant or member of any political party found violating the law will be decisively trailed and charged before the court of law. Also, the Deputy Commissioner of Police, Zamfara State Command, Kabir Abdul Randawa, has assured political parties and residents of the command’s commitment to providing adequate security and ensuring peaceful political activities in the state. He urged all political parties and candidates to shun intimidation, violence and other acts capable of threatening the peace. item.title: NMA raises alarm over doctors’ health, burnout
item.description: By Chinedu Adonu The Nigerian Medical Association (NMA), Enugu State chapter, has called for improved working conditions and greater attention to doctors’ welfare, warning that medical practitioners risk compromising their own health while caring for patients. The state Chairman of the association, Dr Ortuanya Emeka, made the call in Enugu during a press briefing to mark the 2026 Physicians’ Week celebration. Ortuanya said the theme of the celebration, “Saving the Savers — Promoting Physicians’ Well-being and Preventing Burnout, Cardiovascular Disease, and Premature Death,” highlighted the challenges confronting medical practitioners. He said the future of medicine depended not only on professional commitment but also on a healthy and motivated workforce, supportive government policies, adequate healthcare infrastructure, quality medical education and the responsible adoption of modern technology. According to him, doctors routinely work long hours, handle emergencies, make critical decisions and bear the emotional burden of human suffering, often under difficult working conditions. “Unfortunately, most times, if not at all times, we become so committed to our duties to the point of neglecting our own lives,” he said. The NMA chairman stressed that physicians’ well-being should be treated as a practical professional priority rather than an issue discussed only during ceremonial occasions. He urged Governor Peter Mbah, through the Commissioner for Health, Prof. George Ugwu, to strengthen advocacy for safe working conditions and create an environment where doctors could deliver quality healthcare without unnecessary occupational risks. “We must encourage healthcare employers and relevant authorities to recognise that an exhausted workforce cannot be expected to function indefinitely at its best,” he said. Ortuanya also condemned violence against healthcare workers, describing threats, intimidation, harassment and physical attacks on doctors as unacceptable. He said hospitals should provide safe environments for both patients and healthcare professionals, warning that insecurity in medical facilities could undermine effective healthcare delivery. “Our hospitals must be places of healing, not environments in which healthcare professionals fear for their safety,” he said. The NMA chairman further called for sustained engagement with relevant authorities to address issues affecting medical practitioners, including remuneration, career progression, workplace safety, training opportunities and the availability of essential resources. He said improving doctors’ welfare and working conditions was essential to sustaining a motivated medical workforce and ensuring quality healthcare delivery. item.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, October 21, 2026
item.description: The Nigerian Naira maintained relative stability against the United States Dollar across both official foreign exchange windows and the parallel market in early trading on Wednesday, October 21, 2026. At the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM), the Naira opened trading exchanging at approximately N1,330.97 to N1,332.00 per US Dollar. The current spot rate reflects ongoing interventions and foreign portfolio flows sustaining liquidity within the official autonomous market window. Meanwhile, in the unofficial parallel market, street traders and Bureau De Change (BDC) operators across key commercial hubs such as Lagos and Abuja quoted buying rates around N1,365 per dollar and selling rates near N1,380 per dollar. The premium between the official window and the parallel market continues to hover around N48 to N50 per dollar as retail demand for foreign travel, international tuition payments, and non-official commercial imports remains active. At these rates, a $100 bill translates to approximately N133,097 at the official rate and up to N138,000 when purchased through parallel market channels. Market analysts note that FX liquidity conditions remain closely linked to international crude oil receipts and domestic monetary policy measures aimed at stabilising foreign capital inflows. Falae, a former Minister of Finance and traditional ruler of Ilu-Abo in Ondo State, spoke with journalists at the Akure country home of the late elder statesman and former Afenifere leader, Pa Reuben Fasoranti. He said Afenifere was a self-perpetuating and self-regulating organisation in which leadership emerged through an established process rather than through competition for positions. “Leadership chooses itself. A new leader will emerge without any struggle. “It is obvious who the next leader will be, and I hope and pray it will be so this time,” he said. item.title: 2027: DSS uncovers plot against NYSC members, arrests suspects – INEC
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC, Prof. Joash Amupitan SAN, has disclosed that the people behind a plot against the Commission’s Ad Hoc staff, especially Youth Corps members, have been uncovered and arrested and would be prosecuted soon. Prof. Amupitan made the disclosure in Enugu at the South-East Zonal Interactive Meeting with Staff and Readiness Assessment for the 2027 General Election. According to the Commission’s Daily Bulletin, INEC recently identified potential risks to its Ad Hoc staff, “especially Youth Corps members,” and has taken measures to neutralise the threat. He said the people behind the plot were uncovered by the Department of State Services DSS. The INEC Chairman added that the Commission plans to host a Security Conference “very soon” to address other issues relating to election security. On the Commission’s wider security arrangements, he said its partnership with the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security (ICCES) had been reinvigorated and expanded. Prof. Amupitan said INEC was working with security agencies at national and state levels, using its Election Risk Management ERM tools, to develop “a robust, intelligence-driven security architecture.” He also identified a lingering public trust deficit, voter apathy and the rising tide of misinformation and disinformation as the Commission’s greatest challenges. “A single malicious fake news post, an unverified rumour, or a deepfake video can travel across millions of screens in seconds,” he warned. He said false narratives only gain traction when the Commission’s administrative execution falters. “The conduct, competence, and character of our staff in the field are either our strongest defence against fake news, or its biggest catalyst,” he stated. The INEC Chairman said the Commission’s response would be “proactive transparency, swift official communication, and uncompromising operational precision at every polling unit.” On discipline, Prof. Amupitan said, “Partisan leaning, administrative negligence, extortion, or compromised ethics will not be tolerated under my leadership.” He reminded staff that Section 26 of the Electoral Act 2026 requires all staff, Electoral Officers, Presiding Officers, Returning Officers and participating security officials to swear an oath of loyalty and neutrality. “The question governing your actions must never be ‘Who will benefit from this decision?’ The question must always be ‘What does the law require me to do?'” he said. item.title: CVR: INEC reviews registration records, PVC bottlenecks in S’East
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Apparently dissatisfied with the collection rate of Permanent Voters Cards PVCs in the South East, Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC, Prof. Joash Amupitan SAN, has directed that the Commission’s Continuous Voter Registration CVR records in the zone be reviewed and every obstacle to the distribution of PVCs removed ahead of the 2027 General Election. The Commission in its Daily Bulletin said Amupitan gave the directive on Tuesday in Enugu at the South-East Zonal Interactive Meeting with Staff and Readiness Assessment for the 2027 General Election. Prof. Amupitan said the Commission’s “primary operational focus in the South-East is to review our local CVR records and dismantle every bottleneck affecting Permanent Voters Card PVC distribution. “Our objective is uncompromising: no eligible citizen who registered should be disenfranchised by administrative or logistical friction,” he declared. The INEC Chairman noted that the National Register of Voters now stands at over 103 million registered citizens. He recalled that, in line with Section 10 of the Electoral Act 2026, the Commission conducted three structured phases of the CVR. Phase I, which ran from August 25, 2025 to December 10, 2025, registered 2,611,266 voters. Phase II, held between January 5, 2026 and April 17, 2026, registered 4,121,835 voters, while Phase III, conducted from May 11, 2026 to July 26, 2026, registered 3,867,997 voters. According to him, the figures bring the total number of new registrants to 10,772,421 citizens, subject to final Automated Biometric Identification System ABIS deduplication verification at the National Headquarters. On July 20, 2014, Patrick Sawyer, a Liberian-American diplomat who was infected with Ebola, arrived at Murtala Muhammed International Airport in Lagos from Liberia. He was subsequently admitted to a private hospital, where his illness was initially difficult to distinguish from other diseases. He died on July 25, 2014. Eight fatalities from seven laboratory-confirmed Ebola and one probable case were recorded. The deaths included Sawyer and Dr Ameyo Stella Adadevoh, who placed the foreigner in quarantine, as well as six others who were infected during the chain of transmission that followed his arrival. The outbreak was eventually contained, with no new cases reported after August 31, 2014. Nigeria’s latest preparedness efforts began before the reported FCT case. item.title: London/Paris Club refunds: Court voids EFCC probe report
item.description: …Faults FG over probe of ALGON lawyer By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA—A High Court of the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, sitting in Garki, yesterday, set aside an investigation report by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission, EFCC, which alleged fraud in the London/Paris Club refunds involving the 774 local government areas in the country. In the judgment, Justice Suleiman Belgore faulted the Federal Government for directing the anti-graft agency to investigate the matter despite two separate court decisions. The judge held that the Federal Government acted beyond its powers by directing the EFCC, through the Office of the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, to investigate court judgments ordering payment to a consultant, Dr. Ted Iseghohi-Edwards, for legal services rendered in the matter. Justice Belgore noted that the directive came after the government had issued promissory notes for the payment following a clearance report by the Department of State Services, DSS. He held that the EFCC’s subsequent report amounted to an affront to the authority of the court. “The law and the court must be respected. They are both official and statutory. It is not within the powers of the Respondents to use Exhibit GG to impugn the integrity of the court by claiming the judgement was obtained fraudulently,” he held. The judge said the appropriate course for the Federal Government was to file processes seeking to set aside the judgments rather than investigate them. “There were negotiated terms of engagement between the Incorporated Trustees of ALGON and the applicant. These terms of engagement were renegotiated by parties in open court on September 15, 2016,” Justice Belgore added. He held that the 10 promissory notes issued to Iseghohi-Edwards in compliance with a valid order of mandamus made against the Federal Government by the Federal High Court were validly issued by former President Muhammadu Buhari. Consequently, the court upheld the suit filed by the Abuja-based lawyer, holding that there was unassailable evidence that he was retained by the Incorporated Trustees of the Association of Local Governments of Nigeria, ALGON, to represent the 774 local government areas in the London/Paris Club refunds matter. Among the reliefs granted, the court barred the Federal Government and its agencies from arresting, detaining or prosecuting the plaintiff, or infringing on his fundamental rights in connection with the matter. item.title: FG, Bi-Courtney end 20-year MMA2 dispute
item.description: By Folarin Kehinde The Federal Government and Bi-Courtney Aviation Services Limited have signed a final settlement to end a nearly 20-year dispute over MMA2, paving the way for renewed revenue generation and the completion of abandoned hotel and conference centre projects in Lagos. Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, disclosed this on Tuesday in Abuja during the formal signing of the agreement, saying the settlement would enable the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN) to begin receiving concession fees from MMA2 after years of litigation. Keyamo said the agreement followed the approval of the Federal Executive Council and the Federal Government’s decision under President Bola Tinubu to resolve the protracted dispute through negotiations rather than continued court battles. He described the settlement as a reciprocal arrangement under which both parties had agreed to relinquish outstanding claims to establish a framework for future cooperation. He described the settlement as a reciprocal arrangement under which both parties had agreed to relinquish outstanding claims to establish a framework for future cooperation. Keyamo urged Bi-Courtney to fulfil its construction obligations and complete the projects, describing them as potential additions to the aviation and hospitality sectors. item.title: Currency in circulation rises 81% to N5.4trn
item.description: By Peter Egwuatu Currency in circulation in Nigeria rose by 81 per cent to N5.44 trillion in August 2026, from N3.01 trillion in August 2023, underscoring the continued strong demand for physical cash despite the rapid expansion of electronic payments over the past three years. Data from the Central Bank of Nigeria’s, CBN, Money and Credit Statistics show that the strongest increase occurred between August 2023 and August 2024 when currency in circulation rose from N3.010 trillion in August 2023 to N4.55 trillion in August 2024, representing an increase of N1.54 trillion or 51.1 per cent. The growth moderated considerably in the following years. In August 2025, currency in circulation increased to N5.057 trillion, up N508 billion or 11.2 per cent from the previous year. By August 2026, the growth rate moderated further though it hit new threshold of N5.436 trillion, an increase of N379 billion or 7.5 per cent Year-on-Year, YoY. The figures therefore indicate that while the amount of physical cash in circulation has continued to rise, the pace of growth has slowed significantly, from 51.1 per cent in 2024 to 11.2 per cent in 2025 and 7.5 per cent in 2026. Banks’ reserves The increase in currency in circulation occurred alongside a substantial rise in banks’ reserves. According to the data supplied, banks’ reserves rose from N18.528 trillion in August 2023 to N25.456 trillion in August 2024, an increase of N6.928 trillion or 37.4 per cent. They increased further to N31.583 trillion in August 2025, before reaching N36.067 trillion in August 2026. Overall, banks’ reserves increased by N17.539 trillion, or 94.7 per cent, between August 2023 and August 2026. The CBN’s monetary statistics identify currency in circulation and banks’ reserves as components of reserve money or base money. Commenting on the development, David Adonri, Managing Director, High Cap Securities Limited, said: “When more money is held as physical cash, a portion of liquidity is outside the immediate deposit base of commercial banks and is therefore less available for banks to intermediate through loans and other financial assets. However, the rising currency stock should not automatically be interpreted as evidence of excessive liquidity or inflationary pressure. Demand for cash can also increase because of higher nominal prices, larger transaction values and the expansion of economic activity. The increase is particularly noteworthy because Nigeria has experienced rapid growth in electronic payments, mobile banking, fintech services and instant-payment platforms. The continued expansion of physical currency therefore suggests that Nigeria’s digital-payment revolution has not eliminated the country’s cash economy.” Vanguard News The post Currency in circulation rises 81% to N5.4trn appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.description: Governor Dauda Lawal of Zamfara State said Nigerians must learn to live together, support one another and recognise their shared identity, regardless of ethnic or religious differences. The 26-year-old, who has admitted struggling with mental health issues, hadn’t scored for 10 months prior to his goal in Saturday’s win against Ipswich. Long heralded as one of England’s brightest talents, Foden was left out of his country’s World Cup squad earlier this year in a damning sign of his fall from grace. Having ended his run without a goal in the Champions League since November 2025, Foden now has to produce nights like this on a regular basis to complete his revival. Elliot Anderson put City ahead early in the first half with his first goal for the club since his close-season move from Nottingham Forest. item.title: ‘An Icon’: Tinubu, Makinde, Abiodun Pay Tribute To Afenifere Leader Fasoranti
item.description: President Bola Tinubu, Governor Dapo Abiodun of Ogun State, and the Governor of Oyo State, Seyi Makinde, have paid tribute to the leader of the pan-Yoruba socio-political organisation, Afenifere, Reuben Fasoranti, who died on Tuesday. In separate statements, they described Fasoranti’s death as a great “loss”. “I received with profound sadness the news of the passing of Pa Reuben Famuyide Fasoranti, our father, patriarch, elder statesman, and foremost Afenifere leader, who died at the glorious age of 100,” Tinubu wrote in a statement he issued personally. Describing him as “an icon, a beacon of principle, and one of the last great titans of Chief Obafemi Awolowo’s progressive family,” the president said Fasoranti’s life “was a lesson in integrity, discipline, selflessness, and unwavering commitment to the Yoruba people and the unity and progress of Nigeria”. Tinubu said the elder statesman made “immense contributions to this country and, at the risk of his life, fought for the democracy we enjoy today”. “Pa Fasoranti distinguished himself in every respect: in his disciplined, Spartan way of life, his belief in principles, and his commitment to noble causes. Our nation will sorely miss his voice of wisdom, moral authority, and fatherly counsel, especially now, when we need his guidance most,” the president said. “I recall Baba’s centenary on May 11 this year, when we celebrated not just longevity, but a legacy of honour.
